CHIEF COMPLAINT
Routine follow-up with chronic medical conditions and fatigue.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
61-year-old male with history of aortic valve replacement and ascending aortic aneurysm repair on 1/22/2013 presenting for routine follow-up. Patient reports increased fatigue, noting he is unable to maintain his previous cycling pace. Previously able to cycle 40 miles; currently cycles 20-30 miles on a road bike and requires rest afterward. Still cycling regularly but becomes tired and needs to take a break when he gets home. Patient wants to ensure his valve is holding up well, as he is now 8 years out from surgery. He was told at time of surgery the valve would last approximately 8 years. Last stress test was 9/9/2019. Patient denies any drastic changes since last visit. Does not follow up at Hopkins, only gets intermittent follow-ups at this clinic. Wife and friends have noted pursed lip breathing when patient walks; other doctors have mentioned this observation. Denies associated wheezing. Also notes a small nodule on right epididymis that he is not particularly concerned about but wanted to ask about. Denies depression; describes himself as a happy person overall.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient reports increased fatigue at end of day. Denies wheezing. Denies apnea. Reports snoring but wife has not mentioned episodes of not breathing. Gets 6-7 hours of sleep per night. Works out in morning and swims twice weekly at 5:45 AM.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Aortic valve replacement and ascending aortic aneurysm repair on 1/22/2013.

MEDICATIONS
Vitamin D3 50,000 units on Sundays and 2,000 units on other six days. Clindamycin prior to dental procedures.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works and lectures. Exercises regularly by cycling 20-30 miles on road bike and swimming twice weekly. Tries to work out in the morning. Lives with wife. Does not follow up at Hopkins due to stress.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
General: Overall doing well. Respiratory: Pursed lip breathing noted, low exhalation phase, clear to auscultation, no wheezing. Genitalia: Right testicle with 2-3 mm palpable nodule, does not appear to be epididymis or varicocele; left testicle normal; no hernia. All other portions of physical exam normal.

RESULTS
Blood work from 4/10/2021: Alkaline phosphatase elevated at 156, total cholesterol 247, HDL 66, LDL 166, triglycerides 74, TSH normal at 2.68, CBC unremarkable, vitamin D level at high end of normal at 94. Last stress test 9/9/2019.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. History of aortic valve replacement and ascending aortic aneurysm repair: Patient doing well overall and currently asymptomatic. Will obtain echocardiogram and stress test. Referral placed to cardiology (Dr. Vincent Sanchez recommended).

2. Elevated alkaline phosphatase level (156): Likely related to bone health rather than liver. Will order alkaline phosphatase and GGT labs today.

3. Pursed lip breathing with low exhalation phase: Patient reports increased fatigue with cycling. Will order pulmonary function tests for further evaluation.

4. Right testicular nodule (2-3 mm): Referral placed to urology for possible ultrasound.

5. Preventative health: MMR vaccine administered today. Shingles vaccine recommended and will be scheduled for next month. COVID-19 fully vaccinated.

6. Follow-up: Return in one year for wellness visit, sooner if needed. Patient to call with any questions or concerns. Will review all labs and studies and contact patient through patient portal with results unless abnormal findings warrant phone call.
